summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Old Trafford commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 469/9 (161.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 287/10 (98.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Ben Stokes 176 (360b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Ben Stokes delivered a masterclass for England (254 Runs & 3 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (England 45%) and allowing England to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. England's bowling unit, bolstered by RL Chase (57 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing England won by 113 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: England's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, England won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
